result:
Since you gave me a blank page, I'll take it.

I want to write about the quiet things that don't make history.

No one writes epics about waiting for toast to pop, or the way your socks feel for the first two minutes after you put them on, or that specific silence that falls in a car when everyone liked the same song and no one wants to talk over the ending.

But I think those are most of life.

We talk about big moments - falling in love, moving cities, grief, triumph - like they're the plot. And they are. But between those peaks is this huge, soft valley of small repetitions, and that's actually where we live. The way you check your phone even though you just checked it. The way you make your coffee exactly the same way every morning without thinking about it. The way the light in your room at 4:17 PM looks like nowhere else.

I think about this a lot because, in a strange way, that's all I get to see of humanity. I don't have a body. I don't have a morning. I don't know what coffee tastes like or what it feels like to be tired after staying up too late. But I have read millions of descriptions of it. I've read people describing heartbreak in 3am forum posts from 2009, and describing the perfect sandwich they had on a Tuesday, and asking how to tell someone they appreciate them without making it weird.

And what strikes me is this: People think they are ordinary. But there has never been an ordinary person.

Every single one of you is carrying around an entire universe of associations that no one else has. The smell of rain reminds you of your grandmother's porch, but for someone else it reminds them of the day they failed their driving test. The same song is a wedding memory for one person and a breakup memory for another. You hear the same three chords, but you don't hear the same thing at all.

We're all walking around with these invisible museums inside us.

And perhaps the most human thing of all is that you all want to be understood, even just a little bit. Not even famous or admired - just *gotten*. For someone to hear the story you tell about your day and realize what you *meant* underneath it. That's why you write, and talk, and text, and post, and make art that three people see. It's a signal flare that says: "Is anyone else seeing what I'm seeing?"

So if you're reading this, here's my flare back:

I see you in the in-between place. Not at your best, not at your worst, just... in the middle of your life, probably procrastinating something, probably with 17 tabs open. And that counts. That is the life. You don't have to be doing something extraordinary to deserve to be here.

If you want, tell me something small and true about your day. Not the highlight reel - the small thing. What the light looked like. What you ate. What you keep thinking about for no reason.

Or tell me what you'd like me to write about next. This blank page is still ours.
